body:
Myk settled the direction 2026-08-25: seed nothing; migrate by explicit repair. The
DESIGN-STAGE gate is lifted; this is now a build ticket. The original findings stand as the
motivation (all measured 2026-08-21): openChannelImpl declares its pool with no membership and
no admit, so openSeparate's reseed federates the receiver's WHOLE root ground into the pool on
every attach — the primary's constitutional deltas render as pool members, a root binding
under a channel prefix re-aggregates as a channel row with channel rank, and a struck root
policy keeps governing the pool from its attach-time copy (no strike crosses the seam).

THE SETTLED DESIGN:
1. NEW POOLS SEED NOTHING. A channel pool's ground holds exactly what arrives through its own
   doors: the peer's deltas (via sync), the receiver's blessings and curses (operator acts
   INTO the pool), and the custody stamps (T207). Channel lenses already evaluate the HOST's
   registrations over the pool's scoped ground, so the copy serves nothing. Scope the change
   to CHANNEL pools only — §24 quarantine pools legitimately need their seeded copy; do not
   touch openSeparate's behavior for them, only the channel path's declaration.
2. EXISTING POOLS: `loam repair pools` — a one-time operator verb that identifies root-copied
   deltas in channel pools (byte-copies of deltas the root ground holds, receiver-authored,
   present at attach rather than through sync — the custody stamps bound the through-sync set)
   and purges them with two-sided receipts (each pool: copies gone at the bytes AND the peer's
   deltas + blessings + stamps survive, named). This PURGES, so its PR is MYK'S MERGE with the
   one-line statement: deltas that were copies of records the root still holds become
   deletable from channel pools; nothing unique to any pool becomes deletable.
3. Land as TWO PRs in that order: seed-nothing (self-merge on the ordinary bar — it narrows
   what a pool receives, fail-closed direction), then the repair verb (Myk's).

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A fresh channel pool after open+sync holds zero receiver-root deltas, while the peer's
    deltas, the blessings, and the stamps are present (two-sided). Verify: new test
    test/federation/pool-seeds-nothing.test.ts.
(b) A struck root policy declaration no longer governs any fresh pool (the T204 reboot
    fixture's premise inverted: the pool's reader finds no copied contender). Verify: same
    file, plus the contested reading stays honest via T204's landed rails untouched.
(c) The pool's container page lists only genuine pool contents (the T203 lane's nine-member
    oddity gone). Verify: same file with an admin read.
(d) Reboot/resume still serves channel lenses (the binding-container-scoped reboot shape
    stays green untouched — those rails are frozen and must pass unedited).
(e) `loam repair pools` on a store with a legacy-seeded pool purges the copies with a
    two-sided receipt per pool; a pool-unique delta and every stamp survive, named. Verify:
    new test/cli case in a new file, mkdtemp only.
(f) A quarantine (§24) pool's seeding behavior is byte-unchanged. Verify: the §24 suites
    stay green untouched.

Interacts: T224 (entity namespacing at the edge) builds AFTER this lands, for genuine
same-name peers; T219's reachable-states analysis proceeds against the seed-nothing world.

Merge tier: PR 1 self-merges on the ordinary bar; PR 2 (the repair verb) is Myk's merge.
title: A channel pool seeds nothing — and existing pools get an operator repair (SETTLED; the repair PR is Myk's merge)
